q3.text:
Q3. Pointer actions

A Skipped or Failed reason that a different tool or a pack fixes ends with one secondary button that names the destination, such as 'Install script pack'.

Opening a tool keeps the files open and selects that tool in the rail. Installing a pack never retries automatically: the files stay in the list for a new run.

Retry appears only after a wrong password, a timeout or a processing error.

save.text:
Save step

Tools that combine many files into one always open the native save dialog. Toolbox draws no dialog of its own, so the sheet on the Merge board is a placeholder for the system one. It proposes 'lease-agreement-merged.pdf' in the output location.

If the chosen name already exists, Toolbox writes 'lease-agreement-merged-1.pdf' instead, and the result row says so: 'Renamed to avoid replacing lease-agreement-merged.pdf'.

row4.text: PDF Editor: one document, like a viewer

editor.text:
PDF Editor model

One document per window, like Preview or Acrobat. Page thumbnails sit on the left, the page in the middle, and the inspector for the chosen tool on the right.

The edit toolbar is always visible: Organize, Crop, Edit text, Add text, Sign, Fill forms, Marks, Redact, plus More for Flatten, Split, Merge, Bates, Details and opening the Files view.

Edits are a list of changes that you can undo. The original file is never changed. Export a copy writes a new file and is disabled until something changes.

edkeys.text:
PDF Editor keyboard and screen reader

F6 cycles between the toolbar, thumbnails, page and inspector. The toolbar and thumbnail strip use arrow keys, with Home and End.

Every mark on the page is a focusable object with a name, such as 'Text box, Signed on 12 October, page 3'. Arrow keys nudge it, Shift+arrow moves it further, and Delete removes it.

Undo and Redo announce what they changed, such as 'Undid Add text'.

export.text:
Export order and redaction

Export applies changes in a fixed order: fill forms, edit text, overlays, flatten, then redact.

Before a redacted export, the disclosure says what happens. Affected pages become 300 dpi images. Metadata, XMP and attachments are removed. Annotations, form fields and layers on those pages are removed.

A signature is typed or an uploaded picture. It is not a digital signature, and the Sign panel says so.

conv.text:
One file from many

Images to PDF, Merge, Create GIF, App Icon Set, combining a TIFF and Formatted PDF all make one output. Their run button ends in an ellipsis and opens the native save dialog.

Tools that make one file per input use 'Save to' with an example name. A clash gets -1, -2 and so on, and errors stay per file.

row10.text: Settings, packs, shortcuts and the app icon

set.text:
Settings

Settings opens with Cmd/Ctrl+, from anywhere and replaces the tool rail with its sections. Changes save immediately; there is no Save button.

Switches are real switches with labels. Every section is reachable with Tab and arrow keys.

Packs never download without asking. A tool that needs a missing pack names it and its size, then sends you to this screen or installs it in place.

sec1.text:
Lock & Unlock: mode and passwords

The view is File Security and its one tool is Lock & Unlock, so the rail never reads File Security twice. Unlock removes open passwords. A PDF that opens without a password but limits printing, copying or editing is Skipped, with a pointer to Remove Restrictions in the PDF Editor.

Lock and Unlock is a segmented control in the header. Switching keeps the file list, clears both password fields and re-checks every row for the new mode. It is disabled while a batch runs.

The batch password sits at the top of the options with show/hide. Lock adds Confirm under it. A mismatch marks Confirm as invalid with 'Passwords don't match. Type the new password again.' and Run names the reason.

A row's own password opens an inline editor in that row, with Confirm in Lock. Saved rows show 'Own password' with Change and Use batch password. Clearing it shows a status line with Undo.

sec2.text:
Lock & Unlock: intake, flags and results

Files the other mode accepts stay in the list, flagged with a reason and a Won't run tag, such as a .doc in Lock. A banner offers one action to remove every flagged file. Files no mode accepts go under 'N items not added'.

Results use the shared row pattern. Locked or unlocked rows open or show the copy. A warning row says what changed, such as a removed signature or a -1 rename. Skipped rows say why and point to the fix, such as Unlock it first. Failed rows say why and whether the file is fine.

Retry appears only for a wrong password (Try another password, with an inline field) or a processing error. It runs only that file. A missing PDF helper fails PDFs only, and Office files still run.

Show all in Finder or File Explorer opens the destination once for many results.

sec3.text:
Lock & Unlock: local, destination, search

A note in the options says the tool runs on this device with no network, and that passwords are never saved and are cleared on a mode switch or on leaving. Results repeat that passwords were cleared.

Save to defaults to next to each original. Change for this run shows This run only and Reset to default. Copies end in -protected or -unlocked, and nothing is replaced.

Command center: File Security, lock icon. Find a tool matches lock, unlock, protect, password, encrypt and decrypt.

New patterns: the mode segmented control, inline row editors, and flagged rows with a Won't run tag.

row1.text: Finding a tool, adding files, choosing where outputs go

row2.text: Running a batch and reading the results

q8.text:
Q8. Six views and rail scaling

The command center lists the six views as sections with their tools inline. Any tool is one click away, and search is focused with Cmd/Ctrl+K.

Inside a view, the app sidebar becomes that view's tool rail. It's a plain vertical list that scrolls, so 12 or more tools fit without truncation. Short names come from the registry.

Below 980 px the rail turns into a horizontal strip under the header. Tools that don't fit go into a More menu. Arrow keys, Home and End work in both layouts.

q5.text:
Q5. Intake

With no files, the whole center pane is the drop target. Its border becomes solid and its text reads 'Drop to add' while files are dragged over it. Open files is the primary button, with the shortcut beside it. The accepted types are listed under it.

Files that aren't added are collected in a 'Not added' group under the list, each with its reason. A folder, a duplicate and a wrong type each get their own line. A wrong type can point to the right tool. Nothing in this group blocks the run.

q1.text:
Q1. Destination and per-run marking

'Save to' sits in the options panel, just above the Run button, and is always visible. The default reads 'Next to each original' or names the folder.

Change for this run opens the native folder dialog. The changed line gets a 'This run only' badge and a Reset to default link. Leaving the view clears it.

If the folder is missing or can't be written, a dialog appears before anything runs. It offers 'Choose another folder' or 'Save next to originals'. An example output name sits beside the destination line.

q4.text:
Q4. Passwords and overrides

One masked field covers the whole batch. It has a show/hide eye and the note 'Never saved'.

A file with its own password shows a key badge, 'Own password', in the list's Password column. Every other file reads 'Batch password'. The override is set from the row's menu.

After a wrong password, the failed row opens an inline password field and Retry, so only that file runs again.

q7.text:
Q7. Shortcut hints

Hints appear only on the control they trigger, as a small key cap inside the button:
- Open files: Cmd/Ctrl+O
- Run: Cmd/Ctrl+Enter
- Find a tool: Cmd/Ctrl+K
- Settings: Cmd/Ctrl+,
- Cancel: Esc

List hints (Delete removes, Shift or Cmd/Ctrl-click selects) appear as one quiet line above the list once files are added.

All labels switch between Cmd and Ctrl, and between Finder and File Explorer, by platform. Use the Platform tweak on any screen to see both.

q6.text:
Q6. Progress, cancel, locked state

The batch strip at the top of the list shows 'Protecting 7 of 24'. Its bar fills one segment per finished file, coloured by result. Rows switch from Waiting to a spinner to their result as each file finishes, and finished outputs can be opened right away.

The options panel dims, with one line: 'Options are locked until the batch finishes'. The Run button becomes 'Cancel batch' (Esc).

Cancel asks first, saying what is kept and what won't run. Cancelled files become Skipped, with the reason 'Cancelled'.

q2.text:
Q2. Three-state rows and large batches

Each row has an icon, a word and a reason, so the state never depends on colour:
- Succeeded: a check.
- Skipped: a grey dash. It's a no-op, not a problem.
- Failed: a red cross.
Warnings are amber and sit under the output name.

The summary counts double as filters. In large batches, 'Needs attention' groups rows by reason, so 28 'Signature removed' rows become one group you can expand. The list keeps input order.

sr.text:
Screen-reader announcements

One polite live region sits on the batch strip:
- On start: 'Protecting 24 files.'
- During the run: progress every 5 files or 10 seconds, whichever is later, such as 'Protecting, 10 of 24 done.'
- On finish: 'Done. 21 protected, 2 skipped, 1 failed.' Focus stays where it was.

Each row is a list item whose accessible name reads as one sentence: file, state, reason, warnings, then output name. Row actions are real buttons, such as 'Open annual-report-protected.pdf'.

The cancel dialog traps focus and returns it to Cancel batch.

row9m.text: Media creation tools (#634). These boards replace the four Media boards at the left of this row.

m1.text:
Media rail with backlog tools hidden

The rail lists only the four creation tools, in this order: App Icon Set, Create GIF, Extract GIF Frames, TIFF Pages. Blur Faces and Remove Background are hidden, not shown as disabled. They also don't appear in Find a tool, so there are no dead ends.

The rail keeps the shell pattern: All tools, the tools, Settings, and 'Files stay on this device.' Up and Down move between tools. While a run is going, switching tools waits until it finishes.

m2.text:
App Icon Set: layout

Each master image makes its own set, so the files list is the master list. Tags on a row say Not square or Will upscale.

The preview shows the selected master. A segmented control chooses Pad with transparency or Crop to centre. It applies to every non-square master in the run, and images are never stretched. Under it, a contact sheet shows the macOS sizes on the real result. Sizes up to 64 are actual pixels; larger ones are drawn at 96 with their label.

Options: 'Make icons for' is a list of presets (macOS, iPhone and iPad, Android, Website, Custom). Each has a checkbox and a chevron that opens its size grid and container checkboxes: AppIcon.appiconset and ICNS for macOS, appiconset for iOS, favicon.ico for Website.

m3.text:
App Icon Set: unticking a size

AppIcon.appiconset and ICNS need every size in their preset. Unticking one size (64 in the sizeOff state) turns those containers off and disables them. The PNGs for the remaining sizes are still made.

A note explains why: 'need every macOS size, so they're off. Tick 64 to turn them back on.' A 'Tick all macOS sizes' button restores the full set. favicon.ico holds whichever Website sizes are ticked, so it never turns off.

Custom sizes are typed (1 to 4096) and shown as removable chips.

m4.text:
Create GIF: frame strip

Frames are a 6-column grid of thumbnails in play order. Each tile shows its position and delay. Frame 1 is tagged 'Sets size'. Frames that don't match are tagged 'Fitted': they are centred, scaled down to fit and padded with transparency.

'Delay for every frame' (ms) applies to all frames. Selecting a frame shows 'Own delay' for that frame. Clearing it returns the frame to the delay for every frame. Own delays are bold on the tile.

Loop forever is a switch. The preview has Play/Pause and a scrubber. It doesn't autoplay when Reduce motion is on.

Reorder: drag (an insertion bar shows the drop point and the source tile dims) or keyboard. A live status line announces each move.

m5.text:
TIFF Pages: Split or Combine

The mode is a segmented control in the header, like Lock and Unlock. Switching keeps the added files. It is disabled while a run is going.

Split: a file list with page count and format per file, and the selected file's pages below. A 1-page file is tagged Skipped before the run. A file Toolbox can't read is flagged 'Won't run', with a banner to remove flagged files.

Combine: a legend of source files (A, B, C) and one grid of every page across files, each labelled with its source letter and page. Pages reorder like GIF frames. Delete leaves a page out without changing any file. Reset pages restores every page in file order.

Compression: LZW (default), Deflate or None. 16-bit pages stay 16-bit.

m6.text:
Results with many outputs

Each input gets one row. Rows with several outputs have a chevron that expands them: icon sets show their macos, ios and web folders; extracted GIFs show the timings file and the PNG range; split TIFFs show their pages. Groups start collapsed except the first.

Open and Reveal on the group row act on the folder or the first output. Reveal selects all of the group's files. 'Show all in Finder/File Explorer' and 'Expand all' sit above the list.

Create GIF and TIFF Combine make one file, so their result is one row.

m7.text:
Skipped, Failed and where messages appear

Succeeded, Skipped and Failed rows share one list in input order, with the same filters as other tools (All, Needs attention, Warnings). Skipped uses the dash icon in muted text and says why, e.g. 'Only 1 page, so there's nothing to split. No file was made.'

Messages:
- Upscale: a tag on the master row before running, and a warning on the result.
- Bit depth: a hint on the row before running, and a warning on the result.
- Large GIF: a banner above the frames and an amber size estimate in the options.
- Renamed: a warning on the result row naming the file it avoided replacing.
- Unsupported TIFF: flagged 'Won't run' at intake if detectable; otherwise a Failed row naming the page and the compression.

Failures never leave half a set: an icon set or a GIF's frames are saved only when all of them work.

m8.text:
Keyboard

- Cmd/Ctrl+O: add files (Open files).
- Cmd/Ctrl+Enter: run.
- Esc: cancel a run (with the shared confirmation dialog).
- Delete: remove the selected file, frame or page. In Combine it leaves the page out.
- Cmd/Ctrl+A: select all. Shift-click or Cmd/Ctrl-click selects several.
- Frame and page grids: arrow keys move focus, Home and End jump to the ends, and Cmd/Ctrl+Arrow moves the selected items. Each move is announced, e.g. 'Moved IMG_2212.heic to position 3.'
- Results: Up and Down move between rows. Right expands a group, Left collapses it. Enter opens.
- Cmd/Ctrl+K: Find a tool. Cmd/Ctrl+, : Settings.

m9.text:
Destination and save dialogs

App Icon Set, Extract GIF Frames and TIFF Split make outputs per input. They use the shared 'Save to' block with 'Change for this run' and an example name. Icon sets go into a folder per master (app-icon-icons), with a -1 suffix if the folder exists. No save dialog.

Create GIF and TIFF Combine make one file. The run button ends in an ellipsis. The system save dialog opens in the output location: next to the first frame or file by default, or the changed folder. It proposes title-card-animated.gif or cover-combined.tif. A name that's taken gets -1 and a warning. Cancel stops before anything is made.

Names are padded so they sort: 2 digits for pages (-page-01) and 3 for frames (-frame-001).

m10.text:
Changes to earlier notes

These boards replace AppIcons, CreateGif, ExtractGif and TiffPages at the left of the Media row.

The 'One file from many' note lists App Icon Set as a save-dialog tool. Under this design it isn't: each master makes its own folder in the output location, so App Icon Set uses 'Save to' like other per-file tools. The note still holds for Create GIF and TIFF Combine.

ex1.text:
Extract 1. Mode choice, range and per-mode options

Board: Extract from PDF, states Files added, Text options, Images options.

Text / Images / Both is a three-way segmented radio group at the top of the options panel, because it decides everything below it. Both is the default. One hint line under it says what each PDF will produce.

Pages comes next and is the same for every mode: All pages or Range, using the shared range field and hints from PDF to Images.

Below that, one boxed section per part: Text for Text and Both, Images for Images and Both. A section for a part that isn't chosen is hidden, not greyed, and its values are kept if the user switches back.

ex2.text:
Extract 2. Page range and clamping

Board: Extract from PDF, states Page range and Range error.

One range applies to the whole batch. The hint under Pages says it once: pages past a PDF's last page are left out, and a PDF with no pages left is skipped.

The Pages column becomes 'Pages used' and shows '9 of 12' per row, so the clamp is visible before running. A PDF the range shortens gets an amber 'Range shortened' state with the pages that remain.

A PDF the range would empty is not blocked: it runs and ends Skipped with 'No pages in range 3-5, 8-. This PDF has 2 pages.' (results board, Text state).

An invalid range shows the error under the field and disables the run button, with the estimate saying why.

ex3.text:
Extract 3. Folder-per-PDF results

Board: Extract from PDF results, states Both and Images.

There is one row per PDF. Under its name, an outputs list shows one line per output: the text file with Open and Show in Finder, and the images folder with Show in Finder only. In Both mode the text file and the folder share one row.

The folder line carries the counts. Extracted is always shown. Duplicates, small left out and couldn't be saved appear only when they are not zero, joined by middle dots. A renamed folder ('-images-1') says which name already existed.

No thumbnails. A folder can hold hundreds of images, decoding previews would slow the list, and Show in Finder already gives the system's own preview. This keeps the row the same height as every other ResultList row.

ex4.text:
Extract 4. Skipped next to succeeded and failed, and the OCR hand-off

Board: Extract from PDF results, states Both, Text and Needs attention.

Skipped uses the grey dash icon and grey state text. Failed uses the red x. Succeeded uses the check. Skipped rows have no outputs, and the reason says nothing was saved. Both Skipped and Failed count under 'Needs attention', but the segment bar draws Skipped in grey, not red.

In Both mode a PDF that has only one part succeeds with a note: 'Text only' or 'Images only', with the missing part named in the detail.

Open in OCR is the shared pointer button (Q3). It opens OCR with that PDF already in its list, selects OCR in the rail, and keeps the Extract list as it was. It never starts OCR by itself.

ex5.text:
Extract 5. Per-image reports, colour warnings and OCR hints

Board: Extract from PDF results, states Both and Warnings and notes.

The row shows one summary sentence ('3 images weren't saved. 4 pages have no selectable text.') and the state '3 warnings'. A ghost 'Show details (4)' button expands a list beneath the outputs. Each line has its page and image number and a short reason: JBIG2 unsupported, damaged data, over the decoded-size limit, CMYK or inverted JPEG copied as it is, or pages with no selectable text.

Warnings use the amber triangle. OCR hints use the grey info circle. Details start collapsed, so a long report never pushes other PDFs off screen. The Warnings and notes chip filters to these rows and opens their details.

One undecodable image never fails the file. A file fails only when no image could be decoded (Images state, fax-bundle.pdf).

ex6.text:
Extract 6. Where the layout and minimum-size options go, and their defaults

Board: Extract from PDF, states Text options, Images options and Small images skipped.

'Preserve layout' sits in the Text section as a checkbox, off by default. Off means reading order. The hint says when to turn it on: columns and tables.

'Skip small images' sits in the Images section as a checkbox, off by default, so every image is saved, as today. Turning it on shows a number field, 'Smaller than 64 px wide or tall'. The 64 px starting value is a design proposal.

The Images section also says what to expect: JPEG and JPEG 2000 are copied as they are, and everything else is saved as lossless PNG.

ex7.text:
Extract 7. Destination and the per-run change

Board: Extract from PDF, states Files added and Changed save location.

The Save to block is the shared one. It shows the app-wide output location ('Next to each original') and a 'Change for this run' link. After a change it shows the folder, a 'This run only' badge, Change and Reset to default, and a sentence saying the setting itself is unchanged.

The example box under it previews the names for the chosen mode: report-text.txt, and the report-images folder with page-3-image-2.png. It also says that existing names get -1, -2 and so on.

The results panel repeats where outputs were saved and what the run used.

ex8.text:
Extract 8. Errors, keyboard and screen readers

Board: Extract from PDF results, states Both, Text, Images and Helper unavailable.

Password-protected PDFs fail with a Remove Password pointer. Damaged files fail with no pointer. A file over a limit fails with the limit named and a Split PDF pointer when splitting helps (the limit values are placeholders until implementation). A helper timeout fails only that file and offers Retry. A partial publish keeps the saved images as an output and fails the row.

If the text helper is missing, one alert above the list says to reinstall Toolbox, and each row reads 'Unavailable'.

The mode, Pages and per-part choices are radio groups and checkboxes in tab order. The run shortcut, Cancel with Esc and the status lines are the shared ones. Each result row's accessible name is one sentence. Its output buttons name the file, such as 'Open report-text.txt'.

pdrail.text:
Details: rail and names

The PDF Editor rail gets a Details group under its six tools: Privacy Check, Edit Properties and Remove Restrictions. Each name is a verb and what it acts on. The one-line description under the view title is also the rail tooltip.

Remove Restrictions reads 'Lift print, copy and edit limits with the permissions password. Open passwords are removed in File Security.' Unlock in File Security removes open passwords only.

Each tool points at the other instead of doing its job. A permissions-only PDF in Unlock is Skipped with 'Open Remove Restrictions'. A PDF with an open password in Remove Restrictions fails with 'Open Unlock'.

The narrow window shows the three tools as toolbar tabs after an 'Edit PDF and 5 more' menu.

pdq1.text:
Q1. Privacy report: one file and many

Privacy Check is read-only. It never changes or saves a PDF, and results say 'Nothing was changed in any PDF.'

One file: the report replaces the list. A summary counts High, Medium and Low findings and the categories with none found. All 14 categories follow in a fixed order. A category with findings is a card with a severity badge, a count, 'Why it matters', the items, and a pointer when a tool fixes it, such as Open Edit Properties. Empty categories collapse to one line, 'None found'. Unsupported items are always listed, so a report never claims more than was read.

Many files: a report list on the left shows each file with its counts or its failure. The chosen file's report fills the right. A failed file shows its reason and a retry in place of a report.

pdq2.text:
Q2. Copy and save

Copy, Save as JSON and Save as Markdown sit at the top of the report, above the categories, and act on the report on screen. Copy uses Shift+Cmd+C (Ctrl+Shift+C) and copies Markdown.

With many files, an 'All 4 reports' group above the report list has Copy all, Save all as JSON and Save all as Markdown. Failed files have no report and are left out.

Saving writes name-details.json or .md to 'Save reports to'. A taken name gets -1, -2, and the saved banner names the renamed file with Show in Finder (Show in File Explorer). Nothing is written until you choose Save.

pdq3.text:
Q3. Mixed values in a batch

Each field (title, author, subject, created, modified) has Keep, Set and Clear. Under it, 'Now:' summarises the batch, such as '7 different titles, 2 files have none'. Keep leaves each file's own value, even where files differ. Set shows the new value and 'Replaces the title in all 9 files'. Clear says it also removes the XMP copy.

The list shows each file's current title, author and modified date, so differences are visible before the run.

Dates use YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM in local time. An impossible date marks the field invalid, says why with an example, and Run names the reason. While every field is Keep, Run is disabled and says nothing would change.

A file that already matches is Skipped with 'No effective change', and no copy is made.

pdq4.text:
Q4. Batch password, overrides, retries and Skipped

One masked field with show/hide holds the password for all files: the open password in Privacy Check and Edit Properties, the permissions password in Remove Restrictions. It is never saved.

A row's own password opens inline under that row, with 'Use for this file' (Enter) and Cancel (Esc). The row then shows an 'Own password' badge. It is used instead of the batch password for this run only.

After a wrong password, 'Try another password' opens a field in the failed row with 'Retry this file'. Only that file runs again, and its new password isn't saved. A damaged file gets Retry and 'Open Repair PDF'.

Skipped is grey and means nothing needed doing, such as no restrictions or no effective change. It never counts as a failure.

pdq5.text:
Q5. Signature removed

Any save of a signed PDF removes the signature, so Edit Properties and Remove Restrictions warn twice.

Before the run, the row note reads 'Signed. Saving removes the signature.' in amber.

After the run, the row is amber and Saved, not Failed: 'Saved. The digital signature was removed, because changing the file breaks it.' The summary adds '1 saved file has a warning', and the Warnings filter shows it. This is the same sentence File Security uses. Privacy Check only reports the signature and changes nothing.

pdq6.text:
Q6. Destination

Edit Properties and Remove Restrictions show 'Save to' in the options, above Run. Defaults are a folder per tool, such as ~/Documents/Edited and ~/Documents/Unrestricted (C:\Users\Asha\... on Windows). Names add -edited or -unrestricted. A taken name gets -1, -2 and the result row says it was renamed. Originals are never replaced.

'Change for this run' opens the native folder dialog. The new folder applies to this run only and 'Reset to default' turns on so it can be undone. The default changes only in Settings.

Privacy Check shows 'Save reports to', used only when you save reports. The narrow window shows the destination in the list footer, with the same link.

pdq7.text:
Q7. Keyboard and multi-select

The list is a multi-select listbox. Click selects, Shift-click extends, Cmd-click (Ctrl-click) toggles, and arrows move. Delete removes from the list, never from disk. A selection offers 'Set password for 2...' and Remove from list.

Shortcut hints sit on their buttons: Open Cmd/Ctrl+O, Run Cmd+Return (Ctrl+Enter), Cancel Esc, Find a tool Cmd/Ctrl+K, Copy report Shift+Cmd+C (Ctrl+Shift+C).

In reports, arrows move in the report list. From inside a report, Option+Up and Option+Down (Alt+Up, Alt+Down) open the previous or next report.

Keep, Set and Clear are a radio group: one Tab stop, arrows to choose. While a run is going, the list and options are locked and Esc cancels after the current file. The narrow drawer closes with Esc or Done and returns focus to Options.

pdstates.text:
Details boards: states

PdfPrivacy: Files added, Empty, Checking, Report one file, Report batch, Wrong password retry, Reports saved.

PdfProperties: Files added, Empty, One file, Invalid date, All keep, Saving, Results, Wrong password retry.

PdfRestrictions: Files added, Empty, Password shown, Per-file override, Removing, Results, Wrong password retry.

PdfDetailsNarrow: each tool with Files added, Options open and Results, at 900 px.

Every board has dark and light themes and macOS and Windows key labels. SecResults in unlock mode shows the permissions-only PDF that points to Remove Restrictions.

c2pMix.text:
Convert to PDF: one mixed batch

Every added item sits in one list in the order it was added, with a Format column. There are no tabs per format. Word, Excel, PowerPoint, OpenDocument, RTF, older Office (with a Basic fidelity tag), Markdown, pasted HTML, plain text, CSV/TSV and EPUB can share a run.

Options has Page defaults first, then one collapsible section per family that is in the list, in a fixed order. A section disappears when its last file leaves the list, and its choices are kept. Each closed section shows a one-line summary.

Items that can't be added (video, folders) are named in a 'not added' card. Formats that aren't shipped yet (MOBI here) and PDFs stay in the list as 'Not available yet' and 'Will be skipped'.

c2pPaste.text:
Convert to PDF: pasted HTML

Paste HTML… (⌘⇧V, Ctrl+Shift+V on Windows) opens a dialog with a name field and the pasted markup in a monospace box. It shows the size and how many remote images will be left out. Add to list makes a list item with a clipboard icon.

Pasted HTML has no original folder, so when the run starts a native save dialog asks for its name and folder. It opens in the folder last used for pasted HTML, or Documents. That is why the run button ends in an ellipsis while a pasted item is in the list. Cancel returns to the list without converting.

The other files keep saving next to their originals.

c2pRows.text:
Convert to PDF: result rows

Results reuse the shared results header: status title, segment bar, All / Needs attention / Warnings and notes chips, Show all in Finder.

- Fonts: 'Show fonts' expands a list of each font used: embedded, bundled fallback (Calibri to Carlito) or system font.
- Approximate layout and remote content left out use the note icon and say what changed.
- Omitted content (a chart with no stored image) uses the warning icon and amber detail.
- Older Office files carry a Basic fidelity tag.
- Skipped (already a PDF), Failed (password, DRM), Unavailable (MOBI) and Over limit give the reason in the detail line. Password-protected rows point to Open Lock & Unlock.

c2pDest.text:
Convert to PDF: destination

Uses the shared Save to block: next to each original by default, with an example name and -1, -2 for clashes. Change for this run sets a folder for this run only and shows the 'This run only' badge and Reset to default (state: Changed save location).

Pasted HTML is the exception: it asks where to save when the run starts. No original is ever replaced.

c2pCtl.text:
Convert to PDF: Markdown, text and table controls

- Markdown: page size, margins, body font, code blocks (shaded or plain), add a table of contents.
- Plain text: page size, margins, font (monospace default), encoding (Detect, with the detected value named), wrap long lines.
- Tables (CSV/TSV): delimiter (by file type), encoding, first row is a header and repeats on each page, orientation, fit to width.
- Spreadsheets: all sheets or visible only, respect print areas, fit sheet to page width. Presentations: speaker notes, hidden slides (the count is named).

Controls are paired selects and checkboxes inside each section. There is no live preview: the result row's Open shows the real PDF, so there is one render path.

c2pPack.text:
Convert to PDF: script pack

A document whose text needs a script that isn't installed (Devanagari here) gets the shared pack row: package icon, 'Needs a pack', a reason and one 'Install script pack' button with its download size. There is no Retry.

After install the row reads 'Ready to run' with a 'Pack installed' tag. The status line says '1 file is ready to run again' and the run button becomes 'Convert 1 file again'. Only that file runs; PDFs already made are kept.

c2pKeys.text:
Convert to PDF: keyboard and multi-select

The list is a multi-select listbox. Click selects one, Shift-click a range, ⌘-click (Ctrl-click) toggles, ⌘A selects all. Delete or Remove from list removes items from the list, never from disk.

Shortcuts: ⌘O add files, ⌘⇧V paste HTML (new), ⌘↵ convert, Esc cancels a run or closes a dialog. Option sections are buttons with aria-expanded; Enter or Space opens one.

One polite status line announces adds, removals, progress and the final result. Each converts on its own, so one failure doesn't stop the batch.

c2pStates.text:
Convert to PDF: states

ConvertToPdf: Files added (default), Empty, Paste HTML, Markdown options, Plain text options, Table options, Spreadsheet and slide options, Changed save location, Last Markdown removed, Save dialog, Converting.

ConvertToPdfResults: Results (default), Needs attention, Warnings and notes, Script pack installed.

Both boards take theme (dark, light) and platform (macOS, Windows) props.

c2pNew.text:
Convert to PDF: new patterns and open points

- Collapsible option sections are new. There is no shadcn Accordion in the kit, so each header is a Button with aria-expanded and a chevron.
- ⌘⇧V for Paste HTML is a new shortcut. Check it against the global shortcut map.
- The save dialog is drawn as a placeholder. The app uses the native dialog.
- Two states (Table options, Changed save location) show the options panel scrolled.
- The pack size (38 MB) and the unshipped format (MOBI) are illustrative.
- ConvertBatch keeps its older Convert to PDF view until these boards are approved; then remove it.

oc1.text:
OCR 1. Mode, Force and languages

Options run top to bottom: Save as, Languages, Pages, Force, Save to.

Save as is a two-option segmented radiogroup: Searchable PDF (default) or Text file, with a one-line hint under it.

Languages is an ordered list, numbered by priority, with move and remove buttons. English is the default; the last choice is remembered. 'Add a language' is the #445 combobox.

Force is a checkbox, off by default: 'Force: redo earlier OCR text'. Its hint says visible text is always skipped.

oc2.text:
OCR 2. Packs in the picker

Same as #445 (pack=Picker open): one listbox in two groups, 'Installed' and 'Download to use', each pack with its size. English is 'Added' and disabled.

Choosing a pack adds it to the list as 'Not installed' and shows the note 'Hindi needs a 12 MB download.' with Install Hindi. Downloading shows 'Downloading 62%' in the list row (role=status).

A remembered language that is no longer installed is dropped with a notice (state=Pick pages): 'Tamil was removed from your languages.'

oc3.text:
OCR 3. Pages, thumbnails, mixed lists

Pages is a segmented control: All pages (default) or Range, with the shared syntax '1-3, 5, 8-'. One range applies to every PDF and multi-page TIFF and is clamped to each file.

With exactly one PDF, the list becomes a thumbnail listbox (state=Pick pages). Each page carries a class tag: Scan, Text or Earlier OCR. Picks write the range ('1-4, 9', badge 'Set by the page picks'); typing a range updates the picks.

Mixed lists show a Type column (PDF, HEIC photo, TIFF) and a Pages column, and say what each file will do.

oc4.text:
OCR 4. Save to

The shared shell block: 'Save to: Next to each original' with 'Change for this run'. After a change (state=Text file and Force) it shows the folder, the 'This run only' badge, Change and 'Reset to default'.

The Example box follows the mode: site-survey-scan-ocr.pdf or -ocr.txt. Clashes get -1, -2; nothing is replaced.

oc5.text:
OCR 5. Progress

The header counts files and the current page: 'Recognizing file 2 of 9' / 'board-minutes-q3.pdf, page 4 of 9'.

The overall bar counts pages, not files ('35 of 541 pages done'), so a 480-page scan doesn't look stuck.

The active row has its own minibar ('Page 4 of 9'). Waiting rows show their page count. Options lock; Cancel (Esc) keeps finished files.

oc6.text:
OCR 6. Result wording

Searchable / Saved as text: '31 pages recognized. English and Hindi.'
Page detail (toggle, aria-expanded): Recognized: Pages 1-4 and 9 / Skipped, visible text: Pages 5-7 / Skipped, earlier OCR text: Page 8. Turn on Force to replace it.
Warning: 'Signature removed. Adding text removes the digital signature, so the copy isn't signed. The original still is.' (PDF mode only)
Note: 'Saved as 8-bit colour, because the photo is 10-bit.'
Skipped: 'Every page already has text: pages 1-3 visible, page 4 from an earlier OCR run. Nothing was made. Turn on Force…' / 'No pages left in 2-. It has 1 page, so nothing was made.'
No text found: 'OCR completed but found no readable text.' (existing message, kept)

oc7.text:
OCR 7. Errors

InvalidInput (locked): 'It's password-protected. Remove its password in File Security, then run OCR again.' + Remove Password button.
LimitExceeded, state 'Over limit': 'Stopped at page 212 of 480: it reached the time limit for one file. Nothing was saved. Split it into smaller PDFs, then try again.' Limit values are set at implementation.
Unavailable (state=Engine missing): every row 'Unavailable' with 'The text recognition engine is missing. Reinstall Toolbox.' plus one role=alert card. A missing pack is 'Needs a pack' in #445's PackResults.
Each failure stays on its own row.

oc8.text:
OCR 8. Hand-off and shortcuts

Extract from PDF marks a scan 'Needs OCR' with an 'Open in OCR' button. OCR opens with that file queued, a note 'Opened from Extract from PDF' with 'Back to Extract from PDF', and Save as preset to Text file (state=Opened from Extract).

Shortcuts are the shell's: ⌘O / Ctrl+O add files, ⌘↵ / Ctrl+Enter runs, Esc cancels, ⌘K / Ctrl+K, ⌘, / Ctrl+,. No mode shortcut: Tab to Save as, then arrow keys. ⌘A / Ctrl+A picks all thumbnails.

oc9.text:
OCR 9. Playwright states

Empty: run disabled, 'Add files to start'.
Files added: 9 rows, 'loading-spinner.gif wasn't added.', estimate 'This will make up to 7 searchable PDFs'.
Text file and Force: example -ocr.txt, 'Will be skipped' rows, This run only.
Pick pages: listbox aria-multiselectable, range '1-4, 9'.
Opened from Extract, Recognizing (progressbar values, locked fieldset), Results, Text results, Engine missing (role=alert).
Packs: Not installed, Downloading, Picker open (aria-expanded).

oc10.text:
OCR 10. New patterns

Named new patterns: page class tags on thumbnails (Scan / Text / Earlier OCR), the per-row page minibar during a run, the hand-off note from another tool, and the removed-language notice.

All else is the shared shell: grouped rail, Save to, Example, estimate (role=status), ResultList with Skipped and an .outs page-detail sublist.

macOS and Windows differ only in key caps, paths and 'Show in Finder' / 'Show in Explorer'.

cr1.text:
Crop and Resize PDF: one tool, two modes

Crop and Resize PDF is a batch tool in the PDF Editor rail. It works on many PDFs at once and saves new files. The PdfCrop board is different: it crops pages inside the one open document.

The header has a 'Crop pages / Resize pages' switch. It is a radio group, so the arrow keys move between the modes. Switching keeps the files, the Pages range and the Save to choice. Only the mode's own fields change.

The options panel shows only the active mode:
- Crop: Crop by (Rectangle or Margins), then the rectangle or margin fields.
- Resize: Page size, Orientation, Placement.

Pages and Save to come after the mode's fields, in the same place in both modes. The Run button names the mode, such as 'Crop 8 PDFs' or 'Resize 8 PDFs'.

cr2.text:
Drawing the crop and showing margins

Rectangle: drag on the preview page to draw. Eight handles resize it, and dragging inside moves it. During a drag a chip shows the kept size, such as '168 × 241 mm'. The Left, Top, Width and Height fields update live, and typing in them moves the rectangle. Arrow keys move it 1 mm. Shift+Arrow resizes it. Undo and Reset crop sit in the preview header.

The area that will be hidden is shaded. The kept area has a solid edge.

Margins: four edge handles, one per side. Each margin shows its value in a small label on the page, such as '12 mm'. The fields are Top, Right, Bottom and Left. 'Same on all sides' replaces them with one field. The Unit menu offers mm, in and pt.

A negative or empty margin, or margins that leave no area, mark the field as invalid. Run is turned off with 'Fix the margins to crop.'

cr3.text:
One rectangle on mixed page sizes

The rectangle is stored relative to the page, as fractions of its width and height. So it lands in the same spot on any size or orientation. The preview shows it on the selected page. Under 'On other page sizes', small copies show it on a Letter page, a landscape page and the smallest page in the batch, with the size each one keeps.

Margins are absolute lengths, so a small page loses more of its area. The small copies show that. A page with no area left is marked in red: 'No area left. This PDF will fail.' The file row says so before the run, and the footer counts it: 'receipts-q3.pdf will fail on page 3.'

cr4.text:
Resize preview on mixed sizes

The preview shows the chosen page in its new page size. The old page is drawn inside it, and the new page edge is dashed. The caption names both sizes and the scale, such as 'Letter, 216 × 279 mm on A4, 210 × 297 mm. Scaled to 97%.'

Small copies show other sizes in the batch: a landscape page that stays landscape with 'Match page', and a small receipt scaled up to 248%. A page that already has the target size says 'Already A4. Unchanged.' A PDF whose pages in range all match is skipped.

Scale to fit is the default, and nothing is cut off. With 'Actual size, centered', the parts outside the new page are hatched in amber. A warning gives the count: 'Cuts off content on 43 pages.' The footer repeats it.

Custom size accepts 25.4 to 5,080 mm (72 to 14,400 pt). Outside that, the field is invalid and Run is turned off.

cr5.text:
Crop hides, it does not remove

A crop only hides the edges. The content stays in the file and any PDF app can show it again. The Crop options say so in a note under the fields: 'Crop hides the rest of the page. It stays in the file and can be shown again.'

The note ends with a link, 'Remove content with Redact PDF', which opens Redact with the same files. We show the note every time, not as a dialog, so it never blocks a run.

Resize changes the page box and scales the page content. Links, comments and form fields move with the content. Text stays sharp, because nothing is rasterized.

cr6.text:
Pages, page sizes and destination

Pages: one range for every PDF, such as '3-'. Empty means all pages. Pages past the end are ignored. The 'In range' column shows the count per file, such as '12 of 14'. A PDF with no pages in range is skipped.

Page sizes: the file list has a Page size column. It shows the name, such as A4 or Letter, or '2 sizes' when pages differ. The 'Before you run' column notes the outliers, such as 'Page 4 is landscape' or 'Page 3 is 58 × 120 mm'.

Destination: Save to defaults to 'Next to each original'. Names end in -cropped or -resized. A taken name gets -1, -2, and nothing is replaced. 'Change for this run' picks a folder for this run only, shown with a 'This run only' tag. Your default returns when you leave the tool.

cr7.text:
Skipped, failed and signed files

Before the run, the 'Before you run' column states the outcome per file:
- Skipped: no pages in range, or (Resize) already the target size.
- Won't run: password-protected, or over the 1,000-page limit.
- Will fail: margins leave no area on a page.
- Signed, in amber: 'The signature will be removed.'

The footer counts them, such as 'Crops 44 pages in 5 PDFs. 1 will be skipped and 2 won't run.' Run is still on, because each file is handled on its own.

After the run, every row keeps its reason. Failures that another tool fixes end with one button that names it, such as 'Open Remove Password' or 'Open Split PDF'. A signed file is saved, with a warning row and a 'Not carried over' note in the summary panel.

cr8.text:
Scope and assumptions

Two boards: CropResize (ten states) and CropResizeResults (Crop results, Resize results, Running). Theme and platform are props on both.

The tool name is 'Crop and Resize PDF', because Toolbox UI uses 'and', not '&'. The 1,000-page limit and the 25.4 to 5,080 mm size bounds are placeholders. Engineering confirms them.

The batch rules (per-file errors, no overwrites, originals unchanged, the results list and Cancel batch) follow the Running, Results and Split boards.

ic1.text:
Conversion Q1. Ordered list for Images to PDF

ImagesToPdf Files added: a grid of page cards, each with a thumbnail, its page number, name, format and size. The grid reads as the page order.

Reorder by dragging (ImagesToPdf Dragging shows the drop slot and 'Drop here to make floorplan.heic page 2'), by the Move earlier and Move later buttons on each card, or with ⌘/Ctrl+Left and ⌘/Ctrl+Right on the selected card. Sort by: Order added (default), Name or Modified date.

A multi-page TIFF is one wide card numbered 'Pages 5–7' with a thumbnail per TIFF page. Its pages stay together and move as one.

ic2.text:
Conversion Q2. Layout options and the page preview

ImagesToPdf Files added: Page size defaults to Match image, and the only hint is 'Each page is the size of its image. Margin, fit and orientation appear for A4 and Letter.' Margin, fit and orientation are hidden, not disabled, because they do nothing for Match image.

ImagesToPdf A4 layout: choosing A4 or Letter shows Margin (None, Small, Large), Fit (Fit within, Fill the page, trimming edges) and Orientation (Automatic). They are grouped under the page size they depend on.

The page preview appears only for A4 and Letter. It shows the selected page on the paper with its margin, and selecting another card changes it.

ic3.text:
Conversion Q3. Resolution control

ConvertBatch Files added: Resolution, dpi is a segmented control with 72, 150 (default) and 300, plus Custom. Custom (ConvertBatch Range and resolution) shows a number field limited to 72–300.

The hint under it turns the dpi into pixels for a Letter page, such as '1275 × 1650 px' at 150, and says to use 300 for print. Each button has an accessible name such as '150 dpi', so a screen reader does not read a bare number.

ic4.text:
Conversion Q4. Where the image-count estimate goes

ConvertBatch: the estimate sits in the footer, directly above the run button, so it is read last before running: 'This will make 108 images, from 6 PDFs, 1 locked.' The run button points at it with aria-describedby, and it is a polite status region, so changing the range or picks announces the new count.

The list also has an Images column per PDF, so a surprising total can be traced to one file. ConvertBatch Range error replaces the count with 'No image count yet' and disables Convert PDFs.

ic5.text:
Conversion Q5. Page selection across a batch, and clamping

ConvertBatch Range and resolution: one typed range ('3-5, 8-') applies to every PDF. The hint says so: pages past a PDF's last page are left out, and a PDF with no pages left is skipped. Rows show it before running: memo-oct.pdf 'Range shortened, only pages 3 and 4 exist', and cover-letter.pdf 'Will be skipped, no pages in 3-5, 8-'.

ConvertBatch Pick pages: selecting a PDF and pressing Return opens its thumbnails. Picks replace the range for that PDF only, and a badge in the options says so.

ConvertBatch Range error: '5-3 runs backwards. Write it as 3-5.' The error is inline, uses role=alert and is tied to the field with aria-describedby.

ic7.text:
Conversion Q7. Aggregate versus per-file results

Images to PDF makes one file, so ImagesToPdf Combined shows one output card (name, page count, size, Open and Show in Finder) above the list of input images and their pages. In ImagesToPdf Combine failed, nothing is saved. The card names the input and page that stopped it (scan-0042.tiff, TIFF page 2), and every other input says the combine stopped.

PDF to Images and Convert Image Format make files per input, so ConvertBatch Converted and ImageConvert Converted use one result row per input with its own state. A row with several outputs has a Show N images button (aria-expanded) that lists each file with Open and Show in Finder.

ic8.text:
Conversion Q8. The PDF Conversion rail

ConvertBatch Rail and ImagesToPdf Rail: the rail has three labelled groups. Combine and split has Merge PDFs, Split PDF and Images to PDF. From PDF has PDF to Images, Extract from PDF and PDF to EPUB. Make PDFs has OCR, Formatted PDF and Convert to PDF.

Each group is role=group named by its heading. The current tool is aria-pressed. Up and Down move between tools, and Enter opens one, as the Rail state's help line says. Convert Image Format stays in the Images rail (ImageConvert Rail).

ic9.text:
Conversion Q9. Shortcuts and destination

Open files is ⌘/Ctrl+O, run is ⌘/Ctrl+Return (⌘↵ on macOS, Ctrl+Enter on Windows), Find a tool is ⌘/Ctrl+K, and Esc cancels a run. Images to PDF also uses ⌘/Ctrl+Left and ⌘/Ctrl+Right to reorder pages. Every shortcut is shown on its button.

PDF to Images and Convert Image Format show Save to from the app-wide setting ('Next to each original') with 'Change for this run'. After a change, ConvertBatch Range and resolution and ImageConvert Converted show the folder with a 'This run only' badge, Change and Reset to default. The example name shows the suffix: -page-03, or -converted with -p1, -p2 for TIFF pages.

Images to PDF has no Save to. Make PDF… always opens the native save dialog (ImagesToPdf Save dialog), which suggests IMG_4012-combined.pdf next to the first image.

ic6.text:
Conversion Q6. Mixed batch, target, TIFF compression and Skipped

ImageConvert Files added: one list for any mix of HEIC, JPEG, PNG, WebP and TIFF. Each row shows From (format, transparency, bit depth, TIFF page count) and a To column for the chosen target. Files already in the target format say 'Will be skipped, already JPEG' before running. JPG and JPEG count as one format, and so do HEIC and HEIF, and TIF and TIFF.

Per-file notes are predicted before running: 'Transparent areas become white', 'Saved as 8-bit', '3 files, -p1 to -p3'. In ImageConvert format-webp, each row says Lossless or Lossy, quality 90.

Convert to is a segmented control. TIFF compression (LZW default, None, Deflate) appears only when TIFF is the target (ImageConvert format-tiff). There is no quality control. A note says quality is the shared 90 and points to Compress.

A GIF isn't added. A note gives the reason and a button to Extract GIF Frames.

ic10.text:
Conversion: screen reader and platform labels

All three boards follow the same pattern:
- One polite status line under the list header announces changes: 'Added 7 PDFs. 1 file not added.', the new range result, or the drag target.
- Each row's accessible name is one sentence: name, details, state, then the reason, such as 'cover-letter.pdf, 2 pages. No pages in the range, so it will be skipped.'
- The run header is a status region ('Converting PDF 2 of 7'). Progress bars have aria-valuetext ('13 of 88 images saved').
- Errors in fields use role=alert and aria-invalid. A missing renderer is a role=alert card.
- Seg controls are radiogroups with roving tabindex. Locked options use aria-disabled.
- Row actions name their file, such as 'Open logo-converted.jpg'.

On Windows, every board shows Ctrl in place of ⌘, File Explorer in place of Finder ('Show in Explorer' on small buttons), and C:\Users paths. Use the platform prop to see both.

ms1.text:
Merge and Split Q1. Reordering the Merge list

Each row has a grip, its position, a first-page thumbnail, the page count and the size, so files with the same name can be told apart. A repeated file gets a 'Copy 1 of 2' tag (Merge, Files added).

Drag a row by its grip. A 2px insertion line shows where it lands, and a live hint says 'Moving site-photos.pdf to position 2' (Merge, Reordering).

Move up and Move down buttons sit on every row; they are disabled on the first and last row. The keyboard path is Cmd+Up or Down (Ctrl on Windows) on the focused row, shown in the hint and the tooltips. A Sort menu sets name or date order in one step.

With one file, Merge is disabled and says it needs at least 2 PDFs (Merge, One file).

ms2.text:
Merge and Split Q2. Where the output goes

Both boards share one Save to block: the default folder, 'Change for this run' and 'Reset to default' (Merge, Files added; Split, Files added).

Merge makes one file, so Merge opens the native save dialog in that folder with a suggested name, lease-agreement-merged.pdf. Cancel writes nothing (Merge, Save dialog).

Split makes many files, so it saves straight to the folder with no dialog.

Nothing is ever replaced. An existing name gets -1, -2 and so on, and the result says so (Merge, Merged; Split, Results).

ms3.text:
Merge and Split Q3. Split options

Split has two modes in a segmented 'Split by' control: Page ranges and Every N pages. Only the field for the selected mode shows (Split, Files added; Split, Every N pages).

Ranges are typed as 1-3, 5, 8-. Each range becomes one file, and 8- runs to the last page.

Bad input gets one inline alert that names every problem and how to fix it, such as '3-1 runs backwards (write 1-3)'. Split stays disabled with the reason in the footer (Split, Invalid ranges).

The File names section shows example names, such as -pages-1-3 and -page-5.

ms4.text:
Merge and Split Q4. Preview of the page spans

Yes. Each row shows the files it will make as chips before anything runs (Split, Files added; Split, Every N pages).

A range past the last page is shortened (dashed chip) or dropped (struck chip). A PDF is skipped when nothing is left or the result would be the whole file, and the row says why.

A password-protected PDF shows its page count as a dash and says the password must be removed first.

The toolbar and footer total the files to make and the PDFs that will be skipped.

ms5.text:
Merge and Split Q5. Split results

Results are grouped by input PDF, with the output files indented under each group (Split, Results).

Clean groups are folded with 'Show 3 files'. The group row carries the state and the reason: Split, Split with warnings (range dropped, signature removed, bookmarks not kept), Skipped, or Failed.

A PDF that failed part-way lists the parts it saved and offers Retry. A password failure points to Remove Password.

The summary counts double as filter chips, and 'Show all in Finder' opens the folder.

Merge has one output, so its result maps each input to its page range in the merged file (Merge, Merged). If one input fails, nothing is saved (Merge, Failed).

ms6.text:
Merge and Split Q6. Pointer to Organize Pages

Merge joins whole files in order. Removing, rotating or reordering single pages belongs to Organize Pages.

The Merge options panel ends with a short note and an 'Open Organize Pages' button (Merge, Files added). After a merge, open the merged file there to adjust pages.

The pointer stays out of the file list so it does not compete with the main action.

ie1.text:
IE1. Batch vs. preview

The stack always applies to every image in the list. The preview shows one image at a time: the selected row, marked with an eye, is the one previewed, and ↑ ↓ or the arrows above the preview change it (Focused file changed).

The list shows each image's own result size, in → out, so mixed sizes are checked without previewing each one. Without a geometry step the row shows the size and file size instead.

The preview is scaled to fit and is never the saved file. Show original compares against the untouched image.

ie2.text:
IE2. Crop in mixed sizes, and the default

The default is Aspect ratio 4:5, keep Centre. Each image keeps the largest 4:5 area it has, so every size in the batch works and nothing can fail on size. Swap for portrait images flips the ratio for tall photos.

Pixel rectangle (Crop, pixel rectangle) uses one fixed rectangle in source pixels. Images too small for it are marked in the list before running, 'Smaller than the rectangle. Will fail.', and fail on their own in results with 'The crop falls outside this 1200 × 900 image. No copy was made.'

Dragging the area (drag Moving / Resizing) shows the size and position chip and snaps to the centre guides. Arrow keys move it 1 px, Shift+arrow 10 px.

ie3.text:
IE3. How the stack is shown

The six image tools in the rail are the stack. A tool in the stack shows its step number in the rail. The toolbar above the work area shows all six in their fixed run order: Crop, Resize, Rotate and Flip, Colour and Tone, Watermark, Remove Metadata. Steps in the stack are solid chips with a number and ×; the rest are dashed '+ Name' chips that add the step.

The order is fixed, so there is no drag to reorder. Selecting a rail tool or a chip opens its options on the right, headed 'Step N of M' and what it runs after (Step added).

One step is a single-tool edit with that tool's suffix (-cropped, -resized). Two or more save with -edited.

ie4.text:
IE4. Undo, redo and reset vs. Run

Undo and Redo change the stack and step options only, never files. Removing a step or Reset stack shows a status line with Undo (Step removed, Stack reset). Reset stack keeps the image list.

Run is never undone: it writes new files next to the originals and never changes them. After a run the list and the stack stay, so the user can change one step and run again (results, Edit the stack / Run again).

Run is disabled with a reason in the footer when the stack is empty, there are no images, or a value is invalid (Empty, Stack reset, Resize out of range, Watermark unsupported character).

ie5.text:
IE5. Destination

Save to uses the Settings default, 'Next to each original'. 'Change for this run' picks a folder for this run only (Destination this run): the folder is shown with a This run only tag, Reset to default, and a line saying the Settings default stays as it is.

Names are the original name plus the suffix. If the name is taken, -1, -2 and so on is added and the row warns about it in results. Files are never overwritten.

ie6.text:
IE6. Metadata report

Before running: the Metadata tab beside Preview shows what the previewed image contains and what will happen to each kind: Removed, Kept or None found. Orientation and colour profile are always kept.

After running: each cleaned row has 'What was removed', which expands to Removed / Kept / Not found for that file (Metadata removed). A note at the top says profiles and orientation were kept in every copy.

JPEG and PNG are cleaned without re-encoding. HEIC, WebP and TIFF are re-encoded at quality 90, and the row says so. Each copy is re-read after saving; if anything removed is still there, the file fails and no copy is kept.

ie7.text:
IE7. Watermark and PDF parity

The Watermark step uses the same options and words as the PDF watermark: Text or Picture, size as % of width, opacity, colour, angle, and Position (3 × 3 grid) or Tile. The PDF board stays the reference; only the preview differs.

On images the text can be dragged, resized from a corner and turned with the top handle, and it lands in the same relative place on every size (Watermark text, logo tiled).

A character the watermark font can't draw is an error on the field before running (Watermark unsupported character). If it gets through, every file fails in one group in results (Watermark failed).

ie8.text:
IE8. Where notices appear

One rule: a notice sits next to what it is about.

Field errors sit under the field and the Run footer names the fix. Step-level notes (neutral tone, re-encoding) sit at the bottom of that step's options. Format notes (quality 90, transparency flattened) sit under Format (Output format JPEG). Per-file predictions (will fail, will be skipped) sit in that file's row. Files not added sit in a dismissible 'Not added' region above the list (Files added). Stack changes use one status line under the stack.

No toasts. After a run, everything is in the results list, filterable by Needs attention, Warnings and Notes.

ie9.text:
IE9. Skipped vs. success and error

Done: a new file was saved. Done with a warning: saved, but something the user should know (renamed -1, 8-bit, flattened). Skipped: nothing to do, so no copy was made; this is not an error. Failed: the file could not be edited and no copy was made; other files are unaffected.

The two Skipped wordings:
• 'No changes. Already 2048 px on its longest side and already JPEG, so no copy was made.' when the stack would not change the file (also 'No changes. Will be skipped.' before running, Colour and Tone neutral).
• 'No metadata to remove. No copy was made.' when Remove Metadata finds nothing.

Skipped is grey, counts in Needs attention, and never turns the run red.

ie10.text:
IE10. Shortcuts, clashes, macOS and Windows

⌘O / Ctrl+O add files. ⌘↵ / Ctrl+Enter run. ⌘Z / Ctrl+Z undo a stack change; ⇧⌘Z / Ctrl+Y redo (Ctrl+Shift+Z also works on Windows). Inside a text field these keys keep the field's own undo. Delete on a focused chip removes that step; Delete in the list removes that file. ↑ ↓ in the list change the previewed image. Esc cancels a running batch.

No new global keys, so nothing clashes with ⌘K, ⌘, (Settings) or the other views' ⌘E, ⌘D, ⌘/ and F6.

Labels: Show in Finder / Show in File Explorer, Show all in Finder / File Explorer, key hints as above (platform=Windows on every board). Paths use / on macOS and \ on Windows.

ie11.text:
IE11. Progress in large batches

'Editing 9 of 24' with time left, and one segment per file coloured by outcome (Running). Over 60 files the segments become one bar with the same colours in proportion.

The running row says which step it is on ('Step 2 of 3, Resize'). The list shows the latest rows and finished rows stay put, so the list doesn't jump. Each finished file is saved as soon as it is done.

The stack and options are locked during a run with a reason; Cancel batch (Esc) stops after the current file and keeps what is saved.

ie12.text:
IE12. Focus order

Editor: rail → stack toolbar (one tab stop; ← → move between chips, Delete removes, Enter selects) → Undo, Redo, Reset stack → status Undo when shown → Add files, Clear list → Not added region → file list (one tab stop, ↑ ↓) → Preview / Metadata tabs → Show original → preview crop or watermark handle (arrow keys) → step options → Format → Save to → Run.

After removing a step, focus goes to the next chip, or the add chip in its place. After Reset stack, focus goes to the status Undo.

Results: Ran strip → filter chips → Show all → rows (one tab stop, ↑ ↓; Tab reaches Open, Show in Finder and What was removed) → right panel. On finish, focus moves to the headline.

ie13.text:
IE13. Screen reader

The stack is a toolbar with a list 'Steps, in the order they run'. Each chip reads 'Step 1 of 3, Crop' and its × reads 'Remove Crop step'. Rail tools read 'Crop, step 1 of 3' or 'not in the stack'.

Each list row reads name, size in → out, and any warning. The preview has a text alternative describing the crop. Undo and Redo labels include the key.

Stack changes, the run headline and progress are polite live regions; progress announces every 10% and the finish, not every file. Errors are linked to their fields. The Metadata report is a description list.

ie14.text:
IE14. Intake, GIFs and output format

Drop or Open files accepts JPEG, PNG, WebP, HEIC, TIFF and BMP. Others are listed under 'Not added' with a reason: not an image, already in the list, or an animated GIF, which points to Extract GIF Frames.

Format defaults to Keep original format. Choosing JPEG says which images lose transparency and that it saves at quality 90. HEIC and over-8-bit images save as 8-bit sRGB, noted per file.

Images over 16384 px on a side fail on their own with the limit named (Crop and rotate).

ie15.text:
IE15. Narrow window and themes

Below 1000 px the rail becomes a tools strip: the first four tools, then More with Watermark, Remove Image Metadata and the other Images tools (ImageEditNarrow). Step numbers stay on every tool. The stack shows only the steps in it plus '+ Add step'. The file list becomes a Previewing menu.

Every board renders in dark and light (theme=light) and macOS and Windows (platform=Windows) from the same tokens.

cf6.text:
Compress Files: intake, flags, adding and removing

One view takes PDF, JPEG, PNG and WebP in the same batch. With no files the center is the drop zone, Open files (Cmd/Ctrl+O) is the main button, and Medium is already selected. Compress stays disabled with 'Add files to run'.

Each row shows name, folder, type and size. Files known before the run are flagged in place: HEIC gets Will skip and the Convert it to JPEG first reason; a .docx and an animated WebP get Won't run. A banner counts them and offers one action to remove them all.

Adding more appends to the end, scrolls to them and selects them. Duplicates go under Not added. Remove from list (Delete/Backspace) never touches the file; the status line says so and offers Undo.

cf1.text:
Compress Files: Low, Medium, High

Strength is a three-card radio group, Medium by default. Each card has one line on the trade-off, and 'What Medium does' lists what happens per type, so a mixed batch is clear before running.

Low: PDFs are repacked without loss and images inside stay; JPEG is re-saved at high quality; PNG and lossless WebP stay lossless.
Medium: images inside PDFs are recompressed and scaled down; JPEG and lossy WebP at medium quality.
High: lower quality and resolution; PNG cut to 256 colours with dithering; WebP becomes lossy.

Text, transparency and colour profiles always stay. No dpi or quality numbers are shown.

cf2.text:
Compress Files: Strip EXIF

A switch under Strength, off by default. The line under it changes with the state, so the choice is explained where it is made.

Off: camera, date and GPS details stay in the copies.
On: removes them from JPEG, PNG and WebP. Photos stay upright because orientation is applied first. PDFs aren't changed.

The results panel repeats the setting used for the batch.

cf3.text:
Compress Files: Save to

Save to shows the default from Settings: Next to each original, or a folder. 'Change for this run' picks a folder for this batch only; the row then shows This run only, Change and Reset to default, and says Save to goes back afterwards.

Copies end in -compressed. An existing name gets -1, -2 and so on. Originals and existing files are never replaced.

While running, Strength, Strip EXIF, Save to and the list are locked and dimmed, with one line saying why. Progress is per file, finished copies can be opened at once, and Esc cancels the batch.

cf4.text:
Compress Files results: sizes and savings

The summary leads with counts (compressed, skipped, failed), then Saved X, N% smaller, with before and after for the compressed files only. The side panel repeats the batch total and says skipped and failed files aren't counted.

Each compressed row shows before -> after, a small bar of the new size against the old, and the percent saved. Sizes use the platform's units.

The segment bar has one segment per file; for large batches it becomes proportional by outcome.

cf5.text:
Compress Files results: skipped, warned, failed

Compressed: check icon, Open and Show in Finder or File Explorer.
Warning: compressed, with an amber icon and one line on what changed, such as a removed digital signature. It counts as compressed.
Skipped: not an error. The file was fine but no copy was written: no savings (the copy would be larger) or HEIC, with Convert Image Format.
Failed: red, with the reason and the fix. Unsupported type; animated WebP; password-protected (Unlock it first, Open Lock & Unlock); over the page or size limit (Open Split PDF); damaged file; PDF helper missing (a banner, PDFs only, images still run).

There is no Retry: the same file gives the same result. Fix it, then add it again.

cf7.text:
Compress Files results: open, compare, many files

Every compressed row has Open and Show in Finder or File Explorer, labelled with the output file name for screen readers. There is no side-by-side preview; Show in Finder selects the copy so Quick Look or the system viewer compares it with the original.

Show all opens each destination folder once with the copies selected. With This run only, it opens that one folder.

Filters (All, Needs attention, Warnings) show counts, so a 186-file batch can be cut to the 15 that need attention. The list scrolls and rows keep their actions. New batch clears the results.

cf8.text:
Compress Files: command center

One tile, Compress Files, replaces Compress PDF and Compress Images, with the hint 'PDFs, JPEG, PNG and WebP in one batch'. It keeps the compress icon.

Find a tool matches compress, compression, shrink, reduce size, smaller, optimize, PDF, image, photo, JPEG, PNG and WebP.

A favorite on either old tool becomes a favorite on Compress Files, kept in the same place. Recent and pinned entries move the same way.

cf9.text:
Compress Files: keyboard, screen readers, platforms

Tab order: Open or Add files, the list, Remove, Clear list, then Strength (arrow keys move between cards), Strip EXIF (Space), Save to, Change for this run, and the run button. Cmd/Ctrl+Enter runs; Esc cancels a run.

Results: the summary is a polite live region read once when the batch ends. Filters, then rows, each row's Open, Show in and fix button, then New batch.

While running, one polite region reads 'Compressing 6 of 13' at most every few seconds; failures are not read one by one.

macOS shows Cmd shortcuts and Show in Finder; Windows shows Ctrl and Show in File Explorer, and Delete instead of Backspace. Dark and light use the same tokens as the other boards.

ep1.text:
Edit PDF Q1. Grouping: overlays vs document operations

The toolbar groups tools by what they do, split by separators: page operations (Organize, Crop), content edits (Edit text, Add text, Sign, Fill form), range overlays (Watermark, Page numbers, Header and footer), then Redact. More holds Flatten, Split, Merge, Bates and Details.

Overlays put a selectable object on the page. It has a blue outline and the inspector edits it, ending with a Remove action such as 'Remove watermark'. Document operations change pages, so they open their own view (Organize) or act on the whole file. They show no object on the page.

The inspector title always names the active tool.

ep2.text:
Edit PDF Q2. Export summary, fixed order, disabled Export

PdfExport Review lists every contributing change under 'Changes, applied in this fixed order': forms, edit text, overlays, flatten, then redact. Each row names the tool and its pages.

Nothing to export: Export in the header is disabled, and a tooltip explains why: nothing has changed yet, and the run shortcut does nothing.

Export blocked: the Export button is disabled with aria-describedby pointing at the reason, a missing Devanagari script pack. The reason sits directly above the button, with the fix (Install script pack, 38 MB) inside it.

While exporting, the document is locked and the background is aria-hidden. Cancel export (Esc) is the only action.

ep3.text:
Edit PDF Q3. Destination and per-run change

The empty PdfOpen view says copies save next to the original and that another folder can be picked at export.

In the Export dialog, Save to shows the folder. The default is 'Same folder as the original.' PdfExport Other folder shows a changed folder with a 'This export only' badge, a 'Reset to default' button and the hint 'Next export goes back to the original's folder.'

Bates shows the same pattern in its destination bar: 'This run only' and Reset to default. Its empty state shows the default, the same folder as each original. It follows the shared Q1 rule on the Destination board.

ep4.text:
Edit PDF Q4. Form fields, Tab order, required and invalid

Fields show as tinted boxes on the page. The focused field has a blue ring. Required fields have a red asterisk in the label, and the inspector's Fields list shows 'Required, empty'. 'Go to next empty required field' jumps to the next one.

PdfForms Tab order: numbered blue badges 1 to 8 sit beside each field, in the order Tab follows. The checkbox 'Show Tab order on the page' turns them on. Tab order comes from the PDF and is shown, not edited.

PdfForms Invalid entry: the field gets a red border, aria-invalid, and an inline reason ('Not a real date') tied by aria-describedby. The Fields list, the summary and the status line name it too.

ep5.text:
Edit PDF Q5. Typed signature, reuse, reminder

PdfSign Placing: in the typed mode, the name shows in the chosen signature style before you place it. The picture mode uses an image file instead. Either way, you click the page to place it.

PdfSign Use again: signatures already used are listed with a preview. Picking one and clicking the page places it again. 'Placed so far' lists each copy, and each copy can be moved, resized or deleted on its own. New signature and Clear list are below.

The reminder stays visible under the intro in both panels: this is a picture of a signature, not a digital signature. The reuse list points to it with aria-describedby.

ep6.text:
Edit PDF Q6. Range-applied objects

Watermark, page numbers and header and footer are each one object that applies to a page range.

A chip above the page (for example 'Pages 1–14') says which range it covers, with the line 'One watermark, applied to every page in the range. Edit it once, on any page.' Selecting it on any page selects the same object, and every change shows on all pages in the range.

The Pages section in the inspector sets the range: All, Skip the first page, or These pages. The status line confirms how many pages it covers.

ep7.text:
Edit PDF Q7. Token insertion

Header and footer has six labelled boxes: Left, Centre and Right for the header and for the footer. Insert buttons (Page number, Page count, Date, File name) add a token into the box last selected.

Tokens show as blue tags inside the box. They are not typed codes such as {date}, so nobody has to learn a syntax. Backspace removes a whole tag. The page preview shows the filled-in values, such as '3 of 14'.

Bates Stamp text uses the same tag box and Insert buttons: Bates number, File name, Page in file, Date. Stamp text must contain the Bates number.

ep8.text:
Edit PDF Q8. Redaction: mark, search, review, disclosure

Marking: drag over anything to remove. Marks are previews until export, are listed in the inspector, and can be resized or removed.

Search results: 'Find text to redact' lists each match with its page and context. Check the matches to mark, then use Mark selected.

Reviewing: 'Preview as exported' shows marks as solid black. Previous and Next step through every mark, with 'Mark 2 of 5' announced, and Remove drops one.

Export disclosure: a dialog shown before a redacted export. It says which pages become 300 dpi images and that their comments, form fields and hidden layers are removed. Metadata, XMP and attachments go too. Export needs 'I've checked the marks on every page' ticked.

ep9.text:
Edit PDF Q9. Flatten, result warnings, unavailable sub-tool

Flatten confirmation (PdfForms flatten Confirming): a dialog titled 'Flatten fields in the copy?' says what becomes permanent and names the required fields still empty. Its buttons are Keep fields editable and Flatten when exporting.

Result warnings (PdfExport Done with warnings): the copy is saved, and '2 things to check' lists 'Digital signature removed' and 'Font substituted on pages 1 and 3', each with what changed.

Unavailable sub-tool (PdfForms Unsupported form): an XFA form shows a warning in the inspector, explains why, and offers 'Use Add text instead'. Non-editable text (PdfEditText Not editable) offers OCR or Add text.

ep10.text:
Edit PDF Q10. Errors at open

Encrypted PDF (PdfOpen Locked file): the file isn't opened. Unlock in File Security makes an unlocked copy, and the original stays locked.

Limit exceeded (PdfOpen Too many pages): 'court-bundle.pdf is too large to edit' gives the page count and the limit. It offers Split into parts or another PDF. The 2,000-page limit is a placeholder until engineering measures the real ceiling.

Signed file: opens with a warning that exporting removes the digital signature, which the Done-with-warnings result repeats.

Skipped never happens in Edit PDF. It edits one document, so a no-op export is prevented by disabling Export (Nothing to export).

ep11.text:
Edit PDF Q11. Script-pack prompt

Typing text the bundled fonts can't draw (PdfText scriptPackPrompt) shows the text box with a warning in the inspector. The warning names the script and says the box can't be exported until the pack is installed. 'Install script pack' gives the download size and is installed once for all tools.

If you export anyway, PdfExport Export blocked repeats the same message and button above the disabled Export. The wording and the Install action match the optional-pack rows in #445 (Packs, PackResults), so the pack is named the same everywhere.

ep12.text:
Edit PDF Q12. Unexported-changes warning

Closing the window, opening another PDF or going back to All tools with changes that haven't been exported opens 'Export your changes before closing?' (PdfExport Closing with changes). It gives the number of changes and says they're lost on close.

The buttons are Discard changes, Cancel and Export….

The header subtitle keeps a running count, such as '1 change not exported', so the warning is never a surprise.

ep13.text:
Edit PDF Q13. Focus, screen reader, macOS and Windows

Dialogs trap focus and return it to the control that opened them. While a dialog is open, the background is aria-hidden.

Disabled actions point to their reason with aria-describedby: Export, Number files and Export blocked. Status lines are role=status and announce results, such as 'Mark 2 of 5', '3 numbered, 1 failed'.

Platform labels change with the platform property. ⌘ becomes Ctrl, ⌘↵ becomes Ctrl+Enter, ⇧⌘Z becomes Ctrl+Y, Show in Finder becomes Show in File Explorer, and paths use C:\Users\Asha\… with backslashes. Every board renders in both themes.

epb1.text:
Bates Q. File order, preview, ranges, unused gap

Files are listed in numbering order. Each row has a drag grip and Move up, Move down and Remove buttons, so it can be reordered by mouse or keyboard. The Numbers column previews each file's range before anything runs, and the inspector shows an example stamp on a page.

A locked file is flagged before the run. It is skipped and given no numbers, so the set has no gap (Done).

A file that fails during the run keeps the numbers set aside for it, because later files are already stamped. The row shows that range struck through with 'Unused gap', and the banner names it: 'HL000017 to HL000019 are unused.' Copy number list includes the gap.

epb2.text:
Bates Q. Empty, running, results

No files: a drop target with Add PDFs and its shortcut. Number files is disabled with the reason 'Add PDFs first', and the destination reads the same folder as each original.
